card.name: Forms of the verb take
card.fires_on: Forms of "take" (taken, takes, take) and a word right after it in older general prose, where the next words are likely "from", "its", "care", "steps" or "shape".

modes.label: Passive taken
modes.description: The word "taken" after is/be/may be, expecting "from" or "for" next.
modes.example: an arrangement<< taken>> from the outside of the Colosse

modes.label: Takes/take as verb
modes.description: Finite forms of take, often meaning derive or acquire, in historical prose.

modes.label: Word after take
modes.description: A word right after take in an idiom, such as proper, care, no, any, definite.
modes.example: we must take<< care>> to have 350 members;

card.writes: It likely boosts continuations like "from", "with" and "orig" (origin), which fit sources and derivation after take.
card.plain: It marks the verb "take" in phrases like "taken from" or "take care" in old-style prose.
